indicators.note: In part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone's family seat is described as being partly from an ancestral royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, which is the verb sense of romance.

indicators.note: implant says the symbol for boron is put inside the other word

parts.note: in maths a root is a radical
B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: A sci-fi android turns radical after a boron implant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. 'radical' looks like an adjective but means a root in maths.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a humanlike machine, a kind of automaton.

indicators.note: after says the word for look follows the other pieces

parts.note: more means extra
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: An instruction to take care of an extra-large piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as one phrase meaning tend, but 'after' is the placing signal and 'Look' is the old exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The morello is a sour dark cherry, an example of a fruit.

indicators.note: a form of a word is a new shape of it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rusty, rather bleak kind of iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Noir describes dark, pessimistic fiction or film, so it suits something gloomy and grim.

clue.text: Go-getting internee, Pearl, tearing around the city

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go round the city
tearing means ripping apart, so the letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An ambitious prisoner called Pearl races around the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tearing' looks like rushing about but is the anagram signal; 'the city' is Ur, the ancient Mesopotamian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enterprising and business-minded is what an ambitious, go-getting person shows.

indicators.note: about signals that the word for providing is turned round

parts.note: providing means if, as in 'providing it rains'

indicators.note: effervescent means fizzing and bubbling, so the letters of tonic are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone lies about whether a tonic water is fizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IF into FI, and 'effervescent' shuffles TONIC into CTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiction is an invented story, so a falsehood or untruth counts as one.

indicators.note: brewing means making beer by mixing ingredients, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A guide to the basics of brewing Pilsner lager, compared with distilling spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cf' is the abbreviation for compare, here just letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamental truths from which everything else follows are the basics of a subject.

clue.text: Account on agency model in essence is prepared Italian-style

indicators.note: in says the run of pieces goes inside the word for essence

parts.note: the core of something is its essence

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the account abbreviation comes first

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
the Model T was the early Ford car

explanation.surface: An account of an agency model, in essence, is cooked up Italian-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' works as in a down clue, one piece stacked above the next; the Model T was Ford's famous car.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacciatore means hunter-style in Italian: chicken stewed with tomatoes, mushrooms and herbs.

indicators.note: swaggered means strutted about, so the letters are moved around
almost means the word Latin loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A boastful pupil claims to be almost top of the class in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LATIN to LATI; with I, 'swaggered' rearranges those letters into ITIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something initial comes at the start, so it is the first in a sequence.

definitions.meaning: wound up means irritated or provoked
a compass has a magnetic pointer, so it is fitted with one

explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be annoyed, and a compass literally has a needle.

clue.text: Advocate of trade holding back title

indicators.note: holding says the word for trade keeps the other piece inside it

parts.note: to barter is to trade goods

indicators.note: back says the word for the title is read in reverse

parts.note: Sir is a title given to a knight

explanation.surface: A supporter of commerce is said to be withholding a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' looks like a verb or supporter but means a court lawyer, as in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtroom lawyer who pleads cases is an advocate, the British term being this one.

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre, so take the middle letter of Detective

parts.note: rime is a coating of frost

explanation.surface: A question about what the TV detective Jack Frost concentrates on.
explanation.walkthrough: A Touch of Frost was a British TV police drama starring Detective Inspector Jack Frost. The middle letter of 'Detective' is C.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawbreaking is what any police detective investigates, so it is their focus.

indicators.note: on the radio says the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the tail of something is its tip or end

explanation.surface: Something said about Porky the pig's tail on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky' is British rhyming slang: porky pie means lie. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A porky is a fib, and a tall story or fib is a made-up yarn.

clue.text: R-rendition of Celtic air (Like a Long Tail Feather)

indicators.note: a rendition is a performance or version, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A stuttering performance of a Celtic tune whose title is about a long tail feather.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered R of 'R-rendition' joins CELTIC and AIR as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectrices are a bird's long tail feathers used for steering; the adjective describes things relating to them.

clue.text: Appeared to gobble, er, lush spread — such a pity!

indicators.note: to gobble is to swallow, so the word for appeared takes the other letters inside

parts.note: came means appeared, as in 'came into view'

indicators.note: spread means laid out and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone seemed to devour a lavish spread, which was a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a feast but rearranges ER LUSH into RUELSH, which CAME gobbles.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an idiom of regret, saying something is a great pity.

clue.text: Revulsion of empty hangar filled with gold, ornate ring tops

indicators.note: filled with says the next piece goes inside the emptied word
empty means take out all the inner letters of hangar, leaving the outside pair

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: tops means the first letters of the words ornate and ring

explanation.surface: Disgust at an empty aircraft hangar stocked with gold and ornate ring tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' is the heraldic term for gold, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is strong disgust or shock, the same as a feeling of revulsion.

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British orchestral conductor

explanation.surface: A conductor asks for a concert date to be postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like postponing the date, but it is the definition, meaning unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put off is to be flustered or disconcerted, which is what being shaken up in this sense means.

clue.text: Use a needle to wind back bird film?

indicators.note: wind back says the word for using a needle is read in reverse, like rewinding a tape

parts.note: to use a needle is to sew
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Instructions for rewinding a film about a bird with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy picture set in the American West is one genre of movie, hence the question mark.

definitions.meaning: pads out means fills with wordy padding
batter cakes are cooked in a grid-patterned iron

explanation.definitionFit: To waffle is to talk at length with filler, and the grid-shaped breakfast cakes share the name.

clue.text: Last leg, erecting housing for three-year-old event

indicators.note: housing says the answer sits inside the words before it

explanation.surface: Building work on the final stage of a home for a three-year-old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erecting' in a down clue tempts a reversal, but the letters read downwards as printed. The St Leger is a classic British horse race for three-year-olds at Doncaster.
explanation.definitionFit: This Doncaster classic is a flat race open only to three-year-old horses.

clue.text: Notch almost circling rod, used in a certain style of walking

indicators.note: circling says the trimmed word for notch goes round the other piece
almost means the word for notch loses its last letter

parts.note: a nick is a small notch

indicators.note: used means worn and knocked about, so the letters of rod are jumbled

explanation.surface: A notched stick nearly wraps around a rod, as used in a style of walking with poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a weak anagram signal, easily read as part of the definition. Nordic walking is fitness walking with a pair of poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic walking is fitness walking with poles, so the word names that particular style.

clue.text: Might describe toenail wax with local protection

indicators.note: protection says the word for local surrounds the word for wax

parts.note: a local is a British pub, or inn
to wax is to grow, as the moon does

explanation.surface: Treating a toenail with wax under local protection.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is a neighbourhood pub; 'wax' is the moon's growing, not polish.
explanation.definitionFit: A toenail that curves down into the flesh is the common example of this condition.

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A misfit with a loud mobile phone is universally disliked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal' looks like an adjective but is the Hollywood company, Universal Studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal is a Hollywood company that makes movies, so it is an example of one.

indicators.note: broadcast says the word is spoken out loud

parts.note: not fair means unattractive, the opposite of fair-looking

explanation.surface: Someone protests that broadcasting is unfair, then mentions a sweet wrinkly thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fair' looks like a complaint about fairness; it means plain-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit with a sweet taste and a wrinkled, lumpy skin.

definitions.meaning: a baby is a child or offspring, in the legal sense
a problem is a matter for debate or a point of concern

explanation.definitionFit: Children are a person's legal descendants, and a point of contention is also a matter of concern.

clue.text: Like the Channel Islands, having cells for spores

parts.note: as means like
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey

explanation.surface: Something like the Channel Islands has cells for growing spores.
explanation.definitionFit: In fungi, sac-like cells that produce spores are named by this botanical plural.

clue.text: Gallery not good for Christ's sayings

indicators.note: not says the letter for good is removed

parts.note: a loggia is an open-sided gallery or arcade

explanation.surface: A gallery is said to be unsuitable for the sayings of Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Logia are collected sayings attributed to Jesus, a term from biblical scholarship.

clue.text: Fancies cultivated US soil in Louisiana's capital

indicators.note: cultivated soil is dug and turned over, so the letters are reworked
capital means the first letter of the word Louisiana

explanation.surface: Farming dreams about tilling American soil in Louisiana's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but joins the fodder with US SOIL and L, the capital of Louisiana.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancies are imaginings or delusions, which is what false impressions of reality are.

clue.text: United, king and queen stamp about — bizarre

indicators.note: about says the word for stamp goes around the other letters

parts.note: a seal is a stamp pressed into wax
U is an abbreviation for United, as in football team names
R is short for rex, Latin for king
R is short for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Manchester United, the king and the queen stamping about is a weird scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreamlike and strange, like a Dali painting, is bizarre.

indicators.note: lost says the word for against is taken away

parts.note: conscience is one's moral sense of right and wrong
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Losing one's moral sense is said to work against discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A discipline is a field of study, and physics or biology are such academic fields.
